newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian overnight credits soar on govt paper sale.
newsitem.headline: Russian overnight credits soar on govt paper sale.

text.p: Russian interbank overnight credit rates soared on Wednesday as banks, which had set aside rouble assets for government paper auctions, rushed to the market for the national currency, dealers said.
A dealer said banks had transferred more roubles than usual to the GKO discount Treasury bill and OFZ interest-bearing bond auctions, causing a shortage of national currency on the market.

"Banks are used to working on the following schedule -- on Tuesday they send money to the bill and bond auctions and on Wednesday to support liquidity, they attract funds from the market where there are usually roubles galore," the dealer said.
"It looks like yesterday a lot of people sent too much money to the auctions and today everyone had rouble orders from clients."
Banks bid 14.6 trillion roubles total in cash for Wednesday's auctions.
A Natsionalny Rezervny Bank dealer said sharp demand for the rouble started in the afternoon, when banks took credits at offer prices. Later supply disappeared altogether, he said.
The rouble for today and tomorrow settlement also edged up in morning trade, dealers said.
